headline: Spreads And Totals Paid The Bill The Moneylines Ran Up
paragraphs: Sixty three plays went out across 58 graded games, 21 of which the model looked at and declined, and the ledger came back 34-28-1 for a profit of 41.95 on 630 staked. That is a 6.7 percent ROI, which is the betting equivalent of finding a twenty in an old coat. Nothing heroic. Nothing embarrassing. Just a slate that mostly behaved.

Underneath that calm number is a civil war. Spreads went 16-10-1 for 45.44 and totals went 13-7 for 48.17, a 24.1 percent return that did most of the actual work. Then the moneyline book went 5-11 and set 51.66 on fire at negative 32.3 percent ROI. The model expected 52.1 percent there and delivered 31.2. The featured disaster was South Florida at plus 215 with a 15.9 point probability edge, which lost 31-24 while the Over on that same game cashed. One brain, two opinions.

The published top five went 2-3 for a loss of 7.91 against a 61 percent expectation, so the five picks we actually pointed at were the five that misbehaved. Season sits at 93-103-4 across 200 plays, down 112.34, negative 5.6 percent. Strip out the hindsight week and it is 40-25-1 for a 110.47 profit, which is a very convenient way to tell the story and exactly why nobody should trust hindsight grading. Lines moved on 37 plays and only 8 moved our way.
